source.title: SGD in Multiclass Logistic Regression: Sequential Learning and Scaling Laws
source.authors: Konstantinos Christopher Tsiolis; Denny Wu; Christos Thrampoulidis; Murat A. Erdogdu

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Extends scaling-law analysis to a theoretical multiclass logistic-regression setting with Gaussian-mixture data, rather than language models, and reports cross-entropy risk and compute-allocation results.
record.gate_note: The paper's results are for population risk on a synthetic Gaussian-mixture classification problem, not held-out language-model pretraining loss. It discusses neural-language-model scaling laws in the introduction and cites them in related work, but those cited results are not rows. The paper's simulated ODE figures illustrate results that are also stated in theorems; the rows below use the text statements.
record.test_reason: This is a theory paper. It proves cross-entropy risk scaling for K-class linear logistic regression on a synthetic Gaussian mixture with power-law class priors, trained by population gradient flow or online SGD. It invokes the neural LM scaling laws (Kaplan, Hoffmann) as motivation and draws analogies to them. No result measures held-out loss of language models or of neural models in another modality or regime, so no row measures what any version names for the same kind of system. The 'model size' is a PCA sketch dimension m and 'compute' is an assumed model C≍mKt, not parameters and tokens of trained networks. The findings are recorded under fits_no_version rather than as tests of V3, V5 or V7.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that multiclass logistic regression with power-law class priors learns classes sequentially, yielding a three-phase cross-entropy scaling law. A PCA-type capacity restriction gives an approximation-plus-optimization decomposition and compute-optimal choices of sketch dimension and training time. Online SGD inherits these scalings over a noise-limited horizon. They also report that squared-loss training scales worse, and they frame the results as theory connecting to empirical neural scaling laws, not as tests of them.
record.recipe_differences: The study derives results for multiclass logistic regression on Gaussian-mixture data using population gradient flow and online SGD; it is not an empirical language-model scaling-law measurement or reproduction.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported scaling depends on the class-prior exponent α, noise level σ, PCA sketch dimension m, training objective, optimization time horizon, and learning-rate conditions. The paper states that nonzero noise can prevent the dynamics from reaching all phases.

fits_no_version.finding: For K-class logistic regression on a power-law-prior GMM (α>1), gradient flow and online SGD give a three-phase cross-entropy risk: a log K plateau, then (log K)^{2-1/α}·t^{-(1-1/α)}, then K/t. With noise σ>0 this is guaranteed only up to T≍1/σ.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sequential class learning under power-law class frequencies yields power-law cross-entropy decay in a solvable linear classifier.

fits_no_version.finding: A PCA sketch to m dimensions gives risk m^{-(α-1)}·log K + (log K)^{2-1/α}·t^{-(1-1/α)}. Under C≍mKt the optimum is m*∝C^{1/(α+1)} and t*∝C^{α/(α+1)}, with risk ∝(K/C)^{(α-1)/(α+1)}. The paper notes a Gaussian sketch fails to create such a bottleneck.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Compute-optimal capacity and time tradeoffs can be derived in solvable classification models, and the derived split depends on how capacity is restricted.

fits_no_version.finding: Training with squared loss on softmax outputs instead of cross-entropy makes early and intermediate phases last about K times longer and slows convergence to t^{-1/2}.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In solvable models, the training objective changes scaling exponents and phase lengths.

record.problems: The evidence is theoretical and concerns a stylized Gaussian-mixture classification model rather than language models or empirical pretraining runs. Nonzero-noise results are controlled only up to a horizon proportional to 1/σ, and the paper says later behavior is not sharply characterized. Empirical PCA and SGD guarantees require stated sample-size and learning-rate conditions.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-bearing results were left out. Squared-loss multi-output regression results are not included because they report squared-loss risk rather than the cross-entropy behavior covered by the claim.

untested.parts: No held-out LM pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens or compute.
No fits on small runs extrapolated to larger runs.
No LM parameter or token allocation and no Kaplan versus Hoffmann comparison. Only a theoretical sketch-dimension versus time analogue.
No image, video, repeated-data, fine-tuning or transfer models. Only a synthetic linear classifier.
No empirical fitting choices or published-law disagreement. Only proofs in a toy model.

missing.what: Numerical ODE simulations: Fig. 1 shows width and time exponents for m=8–256 (K=2048, σ=0.1, α=2). Fig. 2b shows noisy risk curves deviating from theoretical rates at later times.
missing.versions: none (fits_no_version; curve bending in a toy model)

missing.what: Online-SGD compute-optimal allocation m*, n* and risk (ηC-dependent).
Multi-output linear regression with squared loss: risk ∝ t^{-(1-1/α)}, with a constant plateau and exponential convergence.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked theorem statements in a synthetic linear model to V3, V5 and V7 as if they were empirical tests. Under the same-system rule they bear on no version, so all rows are set to none and no verdicts are given. The reader's V5 'limits_scope' and V7 'supports' labels are dropped. Validation issue: the reader linked R10 to a V3 label even though R10 was not linked to V3. R13's value term may be mistranscribed (K^{-1/2} versus K^{1-1/α} in E.38). A reviewer could reasonably treat this as T3 for V5 if 'other training regimes' is read to include stylized classifiers; I did not, because V5 names model kinds such as image and video models and fine-tuning.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test held-out language-model pretraining loss as a function of parameters, tokens, or compute with the other quantities non-bottlenecked.
Does not fit laws on small runs and compare their predictions with runs orders of magnitude larger.

Studies retained dimension and gradient-flow time or online-SGD iterations as proxies, not language-model parameter counts and pretraining-token counts; does not compare the Kaplan and Hoffmann allocation laws.
Does not compare depth, width, or architecture choices at fixed parameter count.
Tests a theoretical multiclass classification setting, not other modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer.
Compares training objectives in a stylized setting, but does not study empirical fitting choices, published-law disagreements, or systematic curve bending in language-model runs.

rows.note: The theorem gives sufficient learning-rate conditions and a finite time horizon.

rows.subject: K-class logistic regression with squared loss and softmax activation
rows.operation_detail: Trains with squared loss on softmax outputs and evaluates the resulting model using cross-entropy risk.
rows.baseline: Cross-entropy-trained model has R(t) ≍ log K in its early phase
rows.note: This is an alternate training-objective comparison; the early-phase order matches the cross-entropy-trained case.
rows.check: Alternative training objective in a toy model. It is not a fitting or setup choice behind published LM laws (V7), and the plateau order matches the cross-entropy case.

rows.subject: K-class logistic regression with squared loss and softmax activation
rows.operation_detail: Trains with squared loss on softmax outputs and evaluates the resulting model using cross-entropy risk.
rows.baseline: Cross-entropy-trained model has intermediate risk proportional to (log K)²⁻¹/ᵅ · t⁻⁽¹⁻¹/ᵅ⁾
rows.value: RCE(t) ≍ K⁻¹⁄² log K · t⁻⁽¹⁻¹/ᵅ⁾ + t⁻¹⁄² gα((t/K)¹⁄ᵅ), with gα(m) = m¹⁻ᵅ⁄² for 1 < α < 2, log(1 + m) for α = 2, and 1 for α > 2
rows.note: The paper characterizes this as worse scaling than cross-entropy training; it also states that early and intermediate phases last longer by a factor of K when ignoring logarithmic factors.
rows.check: Squared-loss-on-softmax intermediate phase: tail term K^{1-1/α}·log K·t^{-(1-1/α)}, plus a head term. The row's first term reads 'K^{-1/2} log K'; Eq. (E.38) has K^{1-1/α}. This is a toy-model comparison, not a V7 test.

rows.subject: K-class logistic regression with squared loss and softmax activation
rows.operation_detail: Trains with squared loss on softmax outputs and evaluates the resulting model using cross-entropy risk.
rows.baseline: Cross-entropy-trained model has convergence rate K/t
rows.value: RCE(t) ≍ t⁻¹⁄² gα(K), with gα(K) = K¹⁻ᵅ⁄² for 1 < α < 2, log(1 + K) for α = 2, and 1 for α > 2
rows.note: The paper says the squared-loss convergence rate is worse than the cross-entropy-trained K/t rate.
rows.check: Slower t^{-1/2}·g_α(K) convergence under squared loss. This is a toy-model objective comparison, not bearing on any version.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: PCA-sketch logistic regression with α > 1 in the stated compute range
reader_labels.reason: The paper derives power-law compute-optimal choices for retained dimension and training time, with a corresponding risk rate (R9).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The optimized quantities are effective dimension and gradient time or iterations, not language-model parameters and tokens; the results require the stated α, compute, horizon, and learning-rate conditions (R7–R11).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Theoretical multiclass Gaussian-mixture classification with cross-entropy training
reader_labels.reason: The paper proves power-law cross-entropy risk phases for the unsketched and PCA-sketched models, and gives corresponding online-SGD results (R1–R11).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Alternate squared-loss training objective, evaluated by cross-entropy
reader_labels.reason: The reported cross-entropy trajectory differs from that of cross-entropy training, including a slower convergence rate (R12–R14).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Changing the training objective from cross-entropy to squared loss on softmax outputs
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports different cross-entropy risk scaling under squared-loss training, including a slower convergence phase (R12–R14).
